learning_outcomes.text: Know the concepts of stress and strain and their existing relationship.
Identify and evaluate the stress states to which different structural elements are subjected.
Calculate and dimension simple structural elements subjected to static loads under resistance criteria, determining their state of deformation.
Be able to apply experimental methods to analyze stresses and deformations in simple structural elements: Extensometry and Photoelasticity.
Be able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of mechanical engineering.

syllabus_topics: General study of the behavior of deformable solids: Concepts of stress and strain.
Plane Elasticity. Analysis of structural elements subjected to forces: Axial, shear, bending, and torsional. Beam deformations.
Experimental methods for stress and strain analysis: photoelasticity.
Analysis of the elastic behavior of materials
1. Elastic equilibrium equations and concept of stress.
1.2. Concept of stress. Normal and tangential stress.
1.3. Relationship between forces and stresses. Physical meaning.
2.1. Matrix expression of the elastic problem. Stress tensor.
3. Analysis of deformations in a continuous medium.
3.1. Concept of displacement and deformation. Longitudinal and transverse deformation.
3.2. Matrix expression of the elastic problem in deformations. Strain tensor.
5. General formulation of the elastic problem.
6.3. Graphical methods for calculating stresses and deformations. Mohr's circle.
8.2. Applications in the stress analysis of continuous media.
9. Fundamental hypotheses of strength of materials.
10. Determination of forces. Equilibrium of the elastic solid.
teaching_methods: Classroom presentations of concepts and problem-solving
assessment_rules: Continuous evaluation includes Control 1 (25%), Control 2 (25%), Control 3 (35%), and a Lab Practices Test (15%). For students not passing via continuous evaluation, a final exam worth 100% of the final grade will be held in the ordinary call. Students not passing in the ordinary call will take a final exam worth 100% of the final grade in the extraordinary call. The content for each control exam will be based on what has been explained up to that point.
